Admission runs a memory bench. The node issues a nonce and the applicant seals 32 GB of Argon2id output over it for sixty seconds, then repeats weekly on a fresh nonce, so the seat holds only while that RAM stays wired and its throughput lands inside a published band.

Fifty clones need 1.6 TB resident at once: the cheapest 64 GB box runs about 35 dollars a month, near 1,750 monthly, plus fifty weekly benchmarks and a speed check that breaks time-sliced hosts.

River silt builds one terrace per flood season, and a sable keeps one den mouth per home range.
